item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
110
ABPZ20 KNHC 110541
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Norbert, located several hundred miles west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Well Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
Disorganized showers and thunderstorms located more than 500 miles
to the southeast of the Hawaiian Islands are associated with a broad
trough of low pressure. Some gradual development of this system is
possible over the next few days while it moves generally northward
and then meanders to the southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

Central and Western East Pacific:
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure are located several hundred miles southwest of the
southwestern coast of Mexico. Gradual development of this system is
anticipated, and a tropical depression is likely to form by early
next week while it moves generally west-northwestward to westward
over the central and western portions of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Adams

item.description: ...NORBERT STRENGTHENS SLIGHTLY... As of 11:00 PM HST Thu Sep 10 the center of Norbert was located near 16.6, -123.3 with movement W at 15 mph. The minimum central pressure was 996 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 60 mph.

item.description:

BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
1100 PM HST Thu Sep 10 2026
 
...NORBERT STRENGTHENS SLIGHTLY...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.6N 123.3W
ABOUT 975 MI...1565 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
ABOUT 2095 MI...3370 KM E OF HILO HAWAII
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 15 MPH...24 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...996 MB...29.42 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was 
located near latitude 16.6 North, longitude 123.3 West. Norbert is 
moving toward the west near 15 mph (24 km/h) and this general motion 
is expected to continue over the next few days. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 60 mph (95 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Some strengthening is forecast, and Norbert could become a hurricane 
this weekend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 996 mb (29.42 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Thu Sep 10 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 110843
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
1100 PM HST Thu Sep 10 2026
 
Convection has increased and become more organized around Norbert 
tonight, with cloud-top temperatures below -80 C observed within the 
CDO. However, the tropical storm continues to contend with moderate 
westerly wind shear, with the center of the low-level circulation 
located near the western edge of the deep convection. Subjective 
and objective Dvorak intensity estimates have increased this 
evening, ranging from 45 to 59 kt. Given the improving convective 
organization and the higher intensity estimates, the initial 
intensity is set at 50 kt for this advisory. 
 
Norbert is moving westward around 13 kt along the southwestern 
periphery of a mid-level ridge building over the eastern Pacific. 
This general motion with a slightly slower forward speed is expected 
over the next few days as the ridge strengthens and builds westward. 
The forecast becomes more complex by the end of the weekend and into 
next week, as the strength and position of the ridge will likely 
determine Norbert's longer-term track. A stronger ridge would favor 
a west-southwestward to southwestward motion, while a weaker ridge 
would allow Norbert to continue moving westward for a longer period. 
The latest NHC forecast calls for Norbert to turn toward the 
west-southwest by early next week and is similar to the previous 
track forecast.
 
Decreasing wind shear and sufficiently warm sea surface temperatures 
should support gradual strengthening over the next few days, 
although some mid-level dry air immediately west of the cyclone 
could limit the extent of the intensification. Beyond 72 h, a wide 
spread develops in the intensity guidance, in part because the 
eventual track will influence Norbert's intensity. The latest NHC 
intensity forecast has been raised slightly from the previous 
advisory through the next day or so and lies near the upper end of 
the intensity guidance, close to the HCCA and Google DeepMind 
solutions. Given the large model spread, forecast confidence is 
slightly below normal beyond 72 h.
